boards.title: Your First Weekend at Reed College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative, under-21-safe weekend sequence that starts with named Reed landmarks and extends to nearby public gardens and riverfront paths.

cards.title: Start at Blue Bridge
cards.subtitle: Eastern bridge across Reed Canyon
cards.notes: Use this named eastern canyon crossing to orient yourself between campus sides, then continue only on established paths.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable campus crossing over the canyon.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s style guide identifies blue bridge as the eastern bridge across the canyon; Reed’s homepage depicts students walking across it.
cards.access_notes: Follow campus and canyon guidance while moving through the area.

cards.title: Walk Reed Canyon’s established trails
cards.subtitle: 28-acre watershed at the heart of campus
cards.notes: Take a slow daylight walk on established trails, observe wildlife from a distance, and leave the watershed as you found it.
cards.short_summary: A campus watershed with Reed Lake, native plants, and pedestrian crossings.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed describes the canyon as a 28-acre campus watershed with established trails and asks visitors to stay on them, leave no trace, and observe wildlife from a distance.
cards.access_notes: Privately owned by Reed; visitors enter at their own risk. Stay on trails; alcohol and fires are prohibited.

cards.title: Get your bearings at Hauser Library
cards.subtitle: Reed’s library and archives
cards.notes: Locate a study seat, ask at the reference desk for the building map, and save the semester-hour schedule for later.
cards.short_summary: A central academic building with extensive collections and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed’s guidebook lists semester hours and describes the library’s print collection, study space, public workstations, printers, and reference help.
cards.access_notes: Published semester hours vary during breaks and summer; confirm access before going.

cards.entity_name: Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery
cards.title: See what is on view at Cooley
cards.subtitle: In Hauser Library
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition page before heading over, then allow time to view the work without rushing to the next stop.
cards.short_summary: Reed’s campus gallery presents rotating exhibitions and its art collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed states that the Douglas F. Cooley Memorial Art Gallery hosts four major exhibitions annually and houses the college’s permanent art collection.
cards.access_notes: A Reed exhibition page lists public hours as Thursday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; verify the current exhibition and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Plan a meal at Commons Café
cards.subtitle: Gray Campus Center
cards.notes: Review the current menu and weekend service window, then use the dining option that suits your schedule and dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: Reed’s flagship dining location, with changing food stations and weekend brunch and dinner service.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed identifies Commons Café in Gray Campus Center and publishes weekend brunch hours of 10 a.m.–2:30 p.m. plus dinner from 5–7 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Hours are subject to change during academic breaks; Reed directs visitors to check the dining site for updates.

cards.title: Stop by the Reed College Bookstore
cards.subtitle: Lower level of Gray Campus Center
cards.notes: Browse course and campus materials during an open weekday, and check posted announcements before making a special trip.
cards.short_summary: A nonprofit campus bookstore serving Reed’s academic needs.
cards.evidence_claim: The bookstore identifies itself as a nonprofit in the lower level of Gray Campus Center and posts weekday hours.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–5 p.m. and Friday 9 a.m.–4 p.m.; it is closed Saturday and Sunday.

cards.title: Find the Watzek Sports Center
cards.subtitle: Reed campus recreation facility
cards.notes: Locate the facility on the campus map and check with Athletics, Fitness & Outdoor Programs before planning a workout or swim.
cards.short_summary: A campus facility with pool, courts, gyms, studios, and fitness spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed lists an indoor pool, squash and racquetball courts, saunas, weight room, gyms, dance studio, and martial arts room at its sports center.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current building hours and eligibility with Athletics, Fitness & Outdoor Programs before entering.

cards.title: Watch for a Reed Outing Club trip
cards.subtitle: Student-led weekend outdoor activity
cards.notes: Join the club email list, read the weekly trip details, and submit the sign-up form if a listed outing fits your experience.
cards.short_summary: Free student-led outings and skill sessions in the greater Portland area.
cards.evidence_claim: Reed says the student-led club plans weekly outings, provides transportation, and offers trips free to all Reed students.
cards.access_notes: Trip details are emailed weekly; trips normally occur Saturday or Sunday and use a sign-up lottery.

cards.title: Visit Crystal Springs Rhododendron Garden
cards.subtitle: 5801 SE 28th Avenue
cards.notes: Use the garden’s paths for a quiet daylight visit, checking its current admission policy and any weekend event restrictions first.
cards.short_summary: A nine-acre public garden surrounding spring-fed Crystal Springs Lake.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks describes this as a nine-acre public garden with rhododendrons, azaleas, other plants, and a spring-fed lake that attracts birds and waterfowl.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Thursday–Tuesday 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m. and Wednesday 1–5:30 p.m.; some weekend areas may be limited by special events.

cards.title: End with a Sellwood Riverfront Park walk
cards.subtitle: SE Spokane Street and Oaks Parkway
cards.notes: Take the paved or unpaved paths for riverfront views, and keep the visit land-based unless you have planned appropriate water recreation.
cards.short_summary: A public riverfront park with paths, a boat dock, picnic tables, and accessible restrooms.
cards.evidence_claim: Portland Parks lists riverfront views, paved and unpaved paths, a boat dock, picnic tables, and accessible restrooms at Sellwood Riverfront Park.
